This is a very common issue with Beko dishwashers (and many other brands). "Gritty bits" usually indicate that food particles are being recirculated rather than flushed away. This is almost always caused by one of three things: a clogged filter, blocked spray arms, or incorrect loading.

Here’s a step-by-step troubleshooting guide to fix it, ordered from most likely to least likely cause:

### 1. Clean the Filter (Most Common Cause)
Beko dishwashers have a filtration system at the bottom of the tub. If this is clogged, food debris gets stuck and gets sprayed back onto your dishes.
• Locate the filter: Remove all racks from the bottom. You’ll see a cylindrical plastic filter assembly in the center or corner of the floor.
• Remove it: Twist the main filter counter-clockwise to unlock it, then lift it out. There is often a secondary flat mesh filter underneath—remove that too.
• Clean thoroughly: Rinse both filters under warm running water. Use an old toothbrush to scrub away any slimy gunk or gritty bits stuck in the mesh.
• Check the sump area: While the filter is out, look into the hole where it sits. You’ll often find a chunk of food (like bone, corn, or glass shard) lodged there. Remove it with tongs or your fingers.
• Reassemble: Put the filters back in exactly as they were and lock them in place.

### 2. Check the Spray Arms
If the spray arms are blocked, water can’t reach all areas, and debris isn’t being washed away properly.
• Remove the lower spray arm: Unscrew or pull it out (check your manual for the specific method). Look inside the holes for grit, seeds, or plastic bits. Clean with a toothpick or run water through it.
• Check the upper spray arm: Reach up into the top of the tub and spin the upper arm by hand. Ensure it spins freely and isn’t blocked by tall items. Wipe out any debris from its nozzles.
• Reattach securely: Make sure they are snapped back on tightly so they don’t wobble or leak water.

### 3. Check for Food Traps in the Door Seal & Drain Pump
• Door seal/gasket: Wipe around the rubber door seal with a damp cloth. Grit often gets trapped here and falls back into the tub during the cycle.
• Drain pump filter (if accessible): Some Beko models have an emergency drain access panel at the bottom front (behind a small kickplate). If you’re comfortable, open it slowly (have towels ready for water spillage) and check for coins, buttons, or large food bits blocking the impeller. Note: Not all Beko models have user-accessible drain pumps; if yours doesn’t, skip this step.

### 4. Loading & Pre-Rinsing Habits
• Scrape, don’t rinse: Modern detergents need some soil to activate properly. Scrape off large chunks (bones, corn, seeds) into the trash, but do not pre-rinse dishes thoroughly. If you rinse everything clean, the dishwasher may think there’s no dirt and use a shorter/lighter cycle, leaving behind fine grit.
• Avoid overloading: Ensure water can reach all surfaces. Place items so they don’t block the spray arms from rotating.
• Check for "hard-to-clean" items: Items like colanders, mesh strainers, or textured bowls trap grit. Clean these by hand if they consistently cause issues.

### 5. Detergent & Water Hardness Issues
• Use the right detergent: Ensure you’re using a good quality dishwasher tablet or powder (not regular dish soap!). Pods can sometimes leave residue if water is very hard or if the door seal is dirty. Try switching to a powder for a few cycles to see if it improves results.
• Check salt level: If your Beko has a built-in water softener, check the salt reservoir (usually under the filter). If it’s empty, minerals can build up and leave a gritty or cloudy film on glassware. Refill with dishwasher-specific salt if needed.

### Quick Test:
After cleaning the filter and spray arms:
1.  Run an empty cycle with a cup of white vinegar placed upright on the top rack (to clean internal buildup).
2.  Then run a normal wash cycle with heavily soiled pots/pans to flush out any remaining debris.

If the problem persists after these steps, there may be a blockage in the drain hose or a faulty pump impeller inside the machine, which would require professional service.

That explains it perfectly! A stiff upper spray arm combined with clogged nozzles means your dishes weren't getting the high-pressure wash they needed to dislodge that grit. Cleaning those filters and clearing the spray arms should solve 90% of your problems.

Since you've already tackled the mechanical blockages, here are three final checks to ensure your Beko runs perfectly:

### 1. The "Stiff" Upper Arm
You mentioned it was stiff. Even after cleaning the holes, make sure the arm spins freely by hand. If it still feels gritty or resistant when you spin it:
• Check the mounting point: Sometimes debris gets trapped in the central hub where the arm connects to the water supply pipe. Give that area a quick wipe with a damp cloth.
• Limescale buildup: If your water is hard, limescale can build up inside the plastic bearing of the arm itself. If it’s still stiff after cleaning the holes, you might need to soak the entire upper spray arm in white vinegar for 30 minutes to dissolve internal scale, then rinse and reattach.

### 2. Loading Technique (The "Grit" Culprit)
Since you had gritty bits left behind, how are you pre-rinsing?
• Stop scraping too hard: If you scrape off all the food before loading, there’s nothing for the dishwasher enzymes in your detergent to "grab onto." Modern detergents need soil to activate. Just knock off large chunks (like bones or corn cobs) and let the rest stay on.
• Face dirty surfaces down: Ensure plates and bowls are facing the spray arms, not each other. If two plates face each other, they create a "dry zone" where water can’t reach.

### 3. Detergent & Rinse Aid
• Rinse Aid is key: Gritty residue often feels like "film" or "sand." This is usually caused by hard water minerals not being rinsed away properly. Ensure your rinse aid dispenser (usually in the door) is filled to the max line. This helps water sheet off dishes, leaving them spot-free and grit-free.
• Check detergent type: Are you using tablets or powder? If you’re using tablets, make sure they aren’t getting stuck under a large plate lid before the cycle starts. They need to dissolve in the bottom of the tub.

Next Steps:
Run an empty cycle on a hot wash (like "Intensive" or "Auto") with just a cup of white vinegar placed upright on the top rack. This will help flush out any remaining loose debris and descale the interior.

That’s great news! It sounds like the clogged filter and spray arms were the main culprits. Since you don’t pre-rinse, your detergent has plenty of "soil" to activate against, which helps it work more effectively.

To keep that grit-free performance going, here are a few final tips for your Beko:

• Monthly Maintenance: Once a month, run an empty cycle at 70°C with a dishwasher cleaner or a cup of white vinegar in the top rack to prevent limescale buildup inside the machine itself.
• Rinse Aid Check: Even if you aren't seeing spots yet, keeping that rinse aid reservoir full will help water sheet off your glasses and bowls, preventing that "gritty" film from forming as the water dries.
• Filter Inspection: Since you found a lot of grease and food in there, try to give the filter a quick rinse under the tap every 2–3 washes. It only takes a minute but keeps the water flow strong.

If you notice any specific issues with certain types of dishes (like cloudy glasses or burnt-on food), let me know!
